recent_posts.title: Issue #472: How React streams UI out of order — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status issue #472 covers how React streams UI out of order using Suspense and Server Components, explaining boundary markers, template placeholders, staging nodes, and inline scripts. Also featured: Nano Stores 1.3 (a 286-byte framework-agnostic state manager), new ES2025/ES2026 JavaScript features (Promise.try, Set methods, Array.fromAsync), the Datatype OpenType font for inline charts, Perry cross-platform TypeScript compiler, upcoming Node v26.0 with Temporal API, and Astro 6.2 release.

recent_posts.title: Issue #471: A reimagining of JSX from a React core alum — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status issue #471 covers several React ecosystem topics: Redux maintainer Mark Erikson's slide deck from React Miami on React Compiler rendering and optimization; TSRX, a TypeScript language extension described as a spiritual successor to JSX by former React team member Dominic Gannaway, which compiles to React, Preact, Solid, and Ripple; a discussion of Next.js Adapters for simplified deployment; and various links on SSR/RSC with TanStack Start, storing variables in React, and using Claude Code to upgrade Expo SDK versions.

recent_posts.title: Issue #470: TanStack Start rethinks React Server Components — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status issue #470 covers TanStack Start's new React Server Components support with an isomorphic-first approach — RSCs render to streams fetched and cached like data, omitting the `use server` directive by design following recent CVEs. Other highlights include a case for domain-first vertical codebase structure, Salesforce's new Multi-Framework runtime for running React apps on its platform, Bun v1.3.12 with native headless browser automation and `Bun.cron`, Node.js 24.15.0 LTS stabilizing `require(esm)`, and TanStack adding Solid 2.0 beta support.

recent_posts.title: Issue #469: A React optimization case study from GitHub — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status issue #469 covers two weeks of frontend news after an Easter break. Highlights include a GitHub engineering case study on cutting memory usage and interaction latency in their React-powered PR diff view, MDN's migration from Create React App to Lit-based web components, an explainer on signals and push-pull reactivity, Railway's move from Next.js to Vite + TanStack Router, and the Docusaurus 3.10 release — the final 3.x version before Docusaurus 4.

recent_posts.title: Issue #468: Why test IDs are an accessibility code smell — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status issue #468 covers several topics: an argument that data-testid attributes are an accessibility smell and role-based selectors are preferable, Next.js 16.2's new stable Adapter API enabling platform-specific build customization (Netlify, Cloudflare, AWS), TanStack DB 0.6 adding SQLite-backed persistence and offline support, and a roundup of ecosystem links including node_modules bloat causes, AI contribution policies in open source projects, and the Secretlint tool for detecting secrets in repos.

recent_posts.title: Issue #466: What a week: Vite 8.0, RedwoodSDK 1.0, shadcn
recent_posts.summary: A roundup of major releases in the React ecosystem: Vite 8.0 drops Babel and Rollup in favor of Oxc and Rolldown for significant performance gains, adds Wasm SSR support, and browser console forwarding. shadcn/cli v4 introduces agent-friendly 'skills', design system presets, and dry-run support. RedwoodSDK 1.0 launches as a Cloudflare-native, server-first React framework built as a Vite plugin. Vitest 4.1 also ships with Vite 8 compatibility. A study of 500 frontend repos highlights missing timer cleanups and event listener removals as the top memory leak causes.

recent_posts.title: Issue #465: How React’s Activity component helps keep state alive — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status issue #465 covers several topics: a retrospective on Patreon's 7-year migration of 11,000 files to TypeScript in a large React codebase, Kent C. Dodds using Cursor to migrate from Remix v2 to React Router v7, Cloudflare's 'vinext' Next.js fork, iOS home screen widgets in Expo, Inertia.js v3 beta (now requiring React 19 and dropping Axios), a new npm registry browser npmx.dev, and a post-mortem on how Trigger.dev was affected by the Shai-Hulud npm supply chain attack.

recent_posts.title: Issue #464: Cloudflare makes its own Vite-powered Next.js — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status issue #464 covers several major ecosystem updates: the React Foundation has officially launched under the Linux Foundation with Meta, Vercel, and Microsoft on the board. React Native now supports Meta Quest devices. Expo SDK 55 ships with React Native 0.83 and React 19.2, dropping legacy architecture support. Also covered: a deep dive into React Query's queryOptions API, Bun v1.3.10's self-contained HTML build feature, Deno 2.7 release, Tailwind CSS 4.2 new color palettes, and the Navigation API reaching Baseline status across browsers.

recent_posts.title: Issue #463: TanStack Hotkeys, a new cross-platform keyboard toolkit — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status Issue #463 is a curated newsletter covering the React ecosystem, featuring TanStack Hotkeys — a new cross-platform keyboard toolkit from TanStack LLC — alongside other articles, tools, and libraries relevant to React developers.

recent_posts.title: Issue #462: Building bulletproof React components and handling billion-row tables — React Status
recent_posts.summary: React Status newsletter covering production-tested patterns for building robust React components, a technical deep-dive into virtual scrolling for billion-row tables, React Native 0.84 with Hermes V1 as default engine, and new tools including FrankenTUI for embedding terminal UIs in React, Tambo for generative UI, and Ink 6.7 for building terminal apps with React components.
